newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-ECCLESTONE WARNS AGAINST TOBACCO BAN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ECCLESTONE WARNS AGAINST TOBACCO BAN.

text.p: Formula One supremo Bernie Ecclestone said in an Italian newspaper interview on Tuesday that a tobacco sponsorship ban would hit the sport's finances and could lead to cutbacks in races or their transfer to Asia.
"Very few other multinationals are capable of investing as much as cigarette producers," Ecclestone told La Stampa, a newspaper controlled by the Agnelli family who own Formula One team Ferrari.
"If they had to abandon the sport it would be a disaster," he added.

The ban on sponsorship of sporting events by tobacco companies proposed by the British government last month caused concern among racing teams such as McLaren, Benetton, Williams and Jordan who are heavily supported by cigarette manufacturers.

Ecclestone, the head of the Formula One Constructors' Association (FOCA), said the proposed British ban and talk of legislative action in Italy might mean some tracks would lose their right to hold championship races.

"We have the right to cancel any (Formula One) race when the running of the race, for whatever reason, is put in danger," he said. "In this case, as sponsors would no longer get a decent return, we would have to reconsider our programme."
The multi-millionaire Ecclestone said one scenario envisaged cancellation of one of Italy's two Grands Prix at Imola and Monza.
Another would give Asian tracks a greater share of the 16 to 17 annual championship races at the expense of European venues.
"We have to go where there is least difficulty. In this respect, the European races may be no more than four," Ecclestone said.
Similar strong-arm tactics worked earlier this season after the Canadian government proposed a tobacco advertising ban on all sports.

Ecclestone said at the time he had numerous countries asking him for the right to stage races and would not hesitate to drop Canada from the Formula One calendar. The government eventually passed an amendment which excluded the Formula One race.
